key_insight: Instead of relying on repeated sampling, the paper learns a semantic search policy that generates diverse concepts or hints to steer LLM reasoning toward better answers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a scalable test-time compute strategy: train a small reusable policy model to improve the pass@k of larger frozen reasoning models without changing the generator itself.
method: Sample diverse problem-specific concepts, hints, or strategies before answer generation.
Replace naive repeated decoding with a more exploratory concept trajectory that encourages semantic diversity.
Train the concept generator with reinforcement learning so its outputs maximize downstream success of a frozen answer model.
evidence_signal: On hard mathematical reasoning tasks, the trained concept generator improves pass@k over repeated sampling at the same answer-generation budget and transfers to unseen answer models, including a different model family.
watch_item: The approach depends on training and reward design for the concept generator, so gains may be task-specific and require careful evaluation to avoid overfitting to one answer model.
paper_title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
